newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN, MAGGERT LEAD U.S. OPEN AS STORM HALTS PLAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN, MAGGERT LEAD U.S. OPEN AS STORM HALTS PLAY.

text.p: Jeff Maggert, using pinpoint iron shots, fired four birdies on the front nine Saturday to catch second-round leader Tom Lehman halfway through the third round of the U.S. Open before a sudden storm interrupted play.

Maggert, who had finished nine holes, and Lehman, through eight, were tied at five under par when a thunder storm struck Congressional Country Club, halting play and sending the 30,000 spectators running for shelter.
It was the second consecutive day that the championship was halted by weather. Friday's second round was interrupted for two hours, 18 minutes by the threat of lightning.

Veteran Hal Sutton, who eagled the 362-yard eighth hole, and young Stewart Cink were two strokes off the pace, one better than first-round leader Colin Montgomerie, who recovered from a disastrous second rounnd.
Tiger Woods, who has not yet shown the magic here that he used to win the Masters, was six shots off the lead playing the 11th hole when play was halted.
Montgomerie had matched Maggert's four-under-par 31 on the front side, but he bogeyed the difficult 10th hole to stand at two under, three shots behind the leaders.

Maggert, who has struggled on the regular tour this year, birdied the first, third, eighth and ninth holes to catch Lehman, who birdied three of four holes from the fourth, but also bogeyed the long sixth.
South African Ernie Els, who won the 1994 U.S. Open in a playoff, Olin Browne and David Ogrin were all at one-under-par.

Woods started the day with three shaky pars and then double bogeyed the 434-yard fourth, where he drove into rough, pulled his next way left and then missed the green with his third shot, which he had to hit over a tree.

The 21-year-old Woods recovered quickly, however, with a birdie at the next and another at the par-three seventh. But he gave one back at the eighth, where he again drove into Congressional's unyielding rough.
After just missing a birdie at the ninth, Woods birdied the 466-yard 10th -- a converted par-5 -- to stand at one under.

Els, who won the '94 Open in a three-way playoff with Montgomerie and Loren Roberts, began the day one shot off the pace, but he double bogeyed the 235-yard second and never mounted a real threat, although he birdied the eighth just before play stopped.
Woods struggled right from the start, hitting two drives into fairway bunkers but still saving par.
However, at the fourth he had his encounter with a tree that led to a double bogey after a weak chip led to two putts and a six.

Maggert found himself in a similar position to Woods's after an errant second shot on the fourth, but he punched his third shot under the tree and it wound up within three feet of the hole, allowing him to save par.

Browne, who has yet to win in three years on the PGA Tour, got off to one of the fastest starts, making three birdies in four holes. He gave one back at the eighth, a short par 4, but then birdied the 607-yard ninth to make the turn at one under -- well in the hunt.

Ogrin, who has won once in 14 years on the tour, had a roller-coaster front nine. After a bogey and a birdie to start, he went birdie, bogey, birdie, bogey from the fifth through the eighth holes to make the turn at one under.
Cink, who says the difficult U.S. Open conditions suit his game, bogeyed the 235-yard second but immediately recovered with a birdie and then added another birdie at the fifth.
The 24-year-old former college star finished tied for 16th in last year's Open, his first.
Forty-five players had still to complete their rounds when play was suspended.
